narrative.overview:
plane-stats is a dark instrument panel that happens to be a web page. The ground is near-black (#070a0f) with a faint 72px grid that fades out at the edges; three low-opacity orbs sit behind it, fixed and unmoving; every panel floats above that ground as a frosted gauge face — a 160° white gradient at 5.5% falling to 1.8%, blurred, with a hairline of light along its top edge and a faint ring set 5px outside it, like the bezel of a cockpit dial. The header is closed by a 1px dashed line: a runway centerline.

The voice is night-watch quiet. This screen is looked at in a dark room, at a glance, by one person checking what is overhead and what was new today. So the interface never raises its own voice: no illustration, no empty decoration, no second accent. Colour is carried almost entirely by data — Sky Blue for anything the operator can act on or read as a series, Signal Mint for what is live or improving, Emergency Amber for one thing only. Everything else is frosted white at low alpha.

Restraint here is not absence of design; it is the precision of a panel where each mark has a job. Numbers are tabular so they do not jitter as they update. Uppercase is reserved for labels at 0.7–0.75rem with 0.09–0.16em tracking, so the eye can skip them; the MLAT badge is the one tighter exception. Panels are the composition: the page is a vertical stack of gauge faces, and the only thing that moves is the data inside them.
keyCharacteristics: Frosted glass panels over a near-black instrument ground; depth is material, not state.
One cool data hue (Sky Blue), one liveness hue (Signal Mint), one alarm hue (Emergency Amber).
System sans at three registers; mono only for machine strings (hex codes, footer).
Tabular numerals everywhere a value can change.
State changes are colour, border and background — never scale, bounce or translate, except the type-dex card's 2px hover lift.
Local-vs-network is a first-class comparison; stale network data is labelled, never passed off as current.

rules.name: The Rarity Rule
rules.body: Sky Blue never fills a surface except the one selected chip. It marks data and interaction; it is not a background.

rules.name: The Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber means an emergency squawk. No other state, badge or warning may borrow it.

rules.name: The Mint Rule
rules.body: Mint marks liveness or a broken record. It is not a generic success colour and never appears on a static value.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change sets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. A value that shifts the layout when it ticks is a bug.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: No second sans family. If a form control does not inherit the stack, fix the control; do not add a font.

rules.name: The Tracked Caps Rule
rules.body: Uppercase only at 0.7–0.75rem with at least 0.09em tracking. The MLAT badge is the one tighter exception at 0.04em. Body copy and data are never uppercase.

rules.name: The Bezel Rule
rules.body: The 5px-offset outline belongs to .glass panels. Cards, pills, chips and inputs get the inset highlight and nothing else.

rules.name: The No-Lift Rule
rules.body: Hover and focus change colour, border or background. They never change transform, size or shadow. The type-dex card is the one exception: it lifts 2px on hover because the whole card is a link.

rules.name: The Stale Rule
rules.body: A stale network poll never reads as current: every network-derived card shows `-` and names the last good poll; local counts stay live.

rules.name: The Focus-Safe Refresh Rule
rules.body: An auto-refreshing region pauses while focus is inside it, and status changes are announced through a polite live region rather than by replacing the focused content.

dos: Do build every surface from the 160° glass gradient and the 1px Hairline Stroke; a flat fill is only for the Table Well and the selected chip.
Do set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every changing value.
Do open each panel with a tracked uppercase eyebrow and its 2px accent bar.
Do use Sky Blue Dim for focus borders and the hex column, full Sky Blue for links and active state.
Do keep the 640px shell breakpoint and the 720px type-hero breakpoint, and let tables scroll horizontally inside .table-wrap rather than the page.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion — the stylesheet already collapses all animation and transition durations.

Do keep every functional label at 11px or larger, body text at 12px or larger, and both at 4.5:1 or better; the detector's undersized-ui-text and low-contrast rules are the floor, not a style opinion.
Do give every auto-updating region a <caption class="sr-only"> and scope="col" headers, and keep the skip link first in <body>.
Do pause an auto-refreshing region while focus is inside it, and announce only status transitions through a polite live region.
Do render an empty state outside a horizontally scrolling table; a one-line state must not inherit the table's width or scroll.
Do label stale network data: network-derived cards show `-` and `last good poll`; local counts stay live.

Do give every text-sized control a 24×24 hit area (WCAG 2.5.8) by growing its padding into the surrounding whitespace with an equal negative margin: .pager-link, td a, .chart-table > summary, and th .sort (whose padding matches the <th>'s, so the whole header cell is the target). The layout must not move.

Do let the card grid reflow on its own width. .card-group is a container and .cards drops to 2 columns below 30rem and 1 below 10rem, so 200% text collapses the grid instead of clipping every numeral.
donts: Don't leave a bare <a> unstyled: color-scheme: dark hands it Chrome's UA lavender, which is not in the palette. The global a { color: var(--accent) } rule exists for exactly this.
Don't use Emergency Amber for anything but emergency squawks. The poller's stale state is the one exception, and it is a status, not an alarm.

Don't treat the emergency log as an alert. It is an archive of events that happened — the owner's words — so it stays a normal panel at the bottom with no toast, no badge and no assertive live region.
Don't make the whole coverage panel a live region. Announce the status line only; a table that re-announces every 10 s is noise.
Don't put an empty state inside a table row on a narrow viewport. It inherits the table's width and clips; render it as a sibling of .table-wrap.
Don't add scale, translate or bounce transitions. State changes are colour, border and background only. The type-dex card's 2px hover lift is the one exception.

Don't size a card grid by viewport width alone. A fixed 2- or 4-column count clips the content at 200% text on every screen; the container query is what keeps 1.4.10 (Reflow) true. Every .cards needs a .card-group parent, or it has no container to query.
Don't let a form field sit under 16px on a phone. iOS zooms the viewport on focus and never zooms back; the mobile rule at the end of the stylesheet is the floor.
Don't convey a chart's values through title alone, and never ship a chart without its <details class="chart-table"> twin. title does not appear on tap or on focus.

Don't animate the background orbs, or add will-change to them. Every backdrop-filter surface above them re-samples its backdrop each frame: measured 3–5 fps with the drift and 43–61 without, on the Pi. Static orbs are a performance contract, not a style choice.

Don't put backdrop-filter on a .card or the search field. Both only ever sit on a .glass panel, whose backdrop is already blurred, so the second blur is invisible and costs a raster each. Blur belongs to the surfaces that meet the raw body: .glass, .pill, .mark.
Don't fill a panel, card or row with Sky Blue; the selected chip is the single filled accent surface.

Don't place a tooltip inside a .glass panel: backdrop-filter makes the panel the containing block for position: fixed, so the tooltip lands offset and under later panels. Keep it a direct child of <body>.
Don't add a second sans family, a display serif, or an icon set; the inline SVG aircraft mark is the only logo asset.
